latest.question: Deputy Darren O'Rourke asked the Minister for Education and Youth if she will review the increasing use of digital devices in secondary schools from an educational outcome's perspective and a cost to parents/guardians perspective given the move away from digital devices in some countries.
latest.reply:
In May 2026, Minister Naughton communicated directly with all schools and boards of management, clarifying the department's position that there is no requirement for a personal device for junior or senior cycle. Minister Naughton requested schools to be cognisant of the views of parents in relation to the use of digital devices and the associated costs. The Minister stressed the need for schools to engage with all parents not just the Parent's Association before deciding on an approach regarding devices.
Minister Naughton will continue engagement with schools, education stakeholders on the impact of digital technologies on educational outcomes and student wellbeing.
In 2024, the department commissioned the OECD to carry out a literature review and a peer learning event (PLE) on the Impact of Digital Technologies on Student Learning as part of the OECD’s Resourcing School Education for the Digital Age Project.
The outputs from this research were formally published in September 2025. The papers set out the impact of various digital technology tools on education and present key findings as well as strategies to support effective integration.
The findings from PISA 2025 also provide useful context. Irish students reported spending less time using digital devices in school for learning activities than the OECD average and reported lower levels of digital distraction in classrooms. The study also found that 78% of students in Ireland attended schools where mobile phone use was not

latest.question: Deputy Liam Quaide asked the Minister for Education and Youth the number of early intervention classes operating, and the number of places available, in each school year from 2022-2023 to 2026-2027, broken down by county, in tabular form; and her views on the value of early intervention classes to autistic children who have difficulty transitioning to mainstream primary school/primary special school.
latest.reply:
In addition to the supports available through the Access and Inclusion Model, or AIM, programme under the Department of Children, Disability and Equality, my department provides funding for the provision of early intervention special classes for children aged 3 -5 years old with a diagnosis of autism. I have asked the NCSE to provide the detailed information requested directly to the Deputy.
As the Deputy will be aware, the Access and Inclusion Model under the Department of Children, Disability and Equality, enables the full inclusion and meaningful participation of children with additional needs in the Early Childhood Care & Education, or ECCE, programme.
Its goal is to create a more inclusive environment in pre-schools, so all children availing of preschool, regardless of ability, can benefit from quality early learning and care.
There has been a significant increase in resources and supports provided to children with additional needs accessing the AIM programme over recent years. I am happy to report that for 2027; funding has been secured to ensure that approximately 8,450 young children with disabilities and additional needs will have access to the AIM programme.
I also understand that from September 2027, the Access and Inclusion Model for children with disabilities in ECCE will be extended to children under three years old, benefiting an estimated 1,000 young children. This is a direct increase in targeted support for early years disabled children.

latest.question: Deputy Peadar Tóibín asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation to provide, for each department, the expenditure levy amount applied from 2027; the specific measures submitted and approved to meet it; the posts to be supressed, programmes reduced and grants to State agencies reduced; the amount classified as efficiencies versus reductions in services; and if proposals by any department were rejected or remain unagreed.
latest.reply:
The achievement of value for money in public expenditure is a Government priority, supported by a strong agenda for reform and efficiency. Public expenditure must be managed to maximise value for money for the taxpayer and support the delivery of Government priorities within the voted allocation, as outlined in Circular 18/2025 (Value for Money Obligations).
Earlier this year, the Government agreed that additional funding of €646 million would be provided to the Department of Education and Youth in 2026. To accommodate this reprioritisation and deliver on the 2027 ceiling agreed under the Medium Term Fiscal Plan, an Expenditure Levy of €446 million has been reflected in all Budget 2027 funding allocations, with the exception the Department of Education and Youth. A breakdown of the expenditure levy for each Vote Group has been provided to the Deputy.
In April, my Department wrote to other Departments highlighting the Government decision to apply an Expenditure Levy for 2027 and emphasise the need to achieve savings. The levy is not intended as an expenditure reduction exercise, rather, it is designed to encourage more efficient and effective delivery of public services.
In designing the levy, Government’s priority has been to protect a number of essential areas. That includes:
• Safeguarding capital spending to address infrastructure gaps and to ensure we can deliver the National Development Plan;
• Preserving social protection and social housing supports to ensure a strong s

latest.question: Deputy Ciarán Ahern asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation if he will give assurances that 100% of revenue collected through the carbon tax will be ringfenced for climate action measures to facilitate a just transition, and that all unspent carbon tax revenue will be carried over to the following year rather than returned to the Exchequer.
latest.reply:
In Budget 2027, and as set out in the Budget Publication "The Use of Carbon Tax Funds", a total of €1,114 million from carbon tax revenue is being allocated to programmes which support climate measures and ensure the most vulnerable are protected from unintended impacts of the tax.
The Programme for Government 2025 – Securing Ireland’s Future commits to using the carbon tax as a key tool to encourage a shift away from fossil fuels and to invest in a sustainable future. It also commits to continue to use carbon tax revenues to fund social welfare measures, agri- environmental schemes and retrofitting.
Between Budget 2020 and Budget 2026, additional carbon tax revenues have been allocated incrementally each year to programmes to insulate the most vulnerable from increases in the carbon tax and to support decarbonisation and energy efficiency programmes across buildings, agriculture and transport.
More recently, in light of the deviation from the previously scheduled increases to the carbon tax rates, carbon tax allocations will remain in line with those made in Budget 2026. While there is no increase in the amount allocated from the carbon tax in 2026, Government is committed to prioritising those key measures which promote a just transition and is increasing the overall expenditure allocations to these measures through wider State funds.

latest.question: Deputy Maurice Quinlivan asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation if he will commit to meaningful public sector pay talks with the unions representing public sector workers.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 50, 55, 64 and 82 together.
I have always been, and remain, committed to meaningful engagement with public service unions and staff associations in relation to a successor Public Service Pay Agreement.
I am very pleased that, following intensive engagement in recent days, industrial action scheduled for 21 October 2026 has been averted.
In this regard, I am appreciative of the efforts of Mr Kevin Foley, as chair, as well as Mr Owen Reidy and Ms Oonagh Buckley in engaging with both parties to identify a pathway back to formal negotiations.
The first formal engagement between the parties took place in the Workplace Relations Commission on 19 October 2026. This represents a constructive step forward and will support efforts to secure a new agreement. There is now a genuine opportunity to make progress through constructive engagement and a shared commitment to dialogue.
I recognise the significant contribution made by public service workers to our society and our country. They are the backbone of our healthcare, social care, education, policing and many other essential services. The Government is committed to negotiating a pay agreement that is fair, affordable and sustainable. However, given the confidential nature of the process, I am not in a position to comment further on the substance of the ongoing discussions or the terms of any potential agreement.

latest.question: Deputy Peter Roche asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation the measures being taken to ensure that the continued digitalisation of public services does not disadvantage older people, people with disabilities or those with limited digital literacy; and the way in which access to in-person and telephone services will be maintained where needed.
latest.reply:
The strategic goal to digitalise public services carries with it a risk of excluding people from participating fully with these services, if their individual needs and preferences are not factored in to the design of these digital-first, but not digital-only, services.
Work to develop the Life Events model for Irish public services so far has included engagement across a range of users with amplified needs when engaging with public services. This has included research with older adults and adults with intellectual disabilities to understand their preferences, challenges and needs when engaging digitally with the State. Understanding the experience of such users is the primary starting point for building out public services, recognising that access is dependent on having the requisite skills, and knowledge, and also the availability of material resources and connectivity.
This approach has allowed the work to move beyond merely increasing digitisation and toward a more holistic set of digitally enabled services that can be accessed across multiple channels, including over the telephone and are centered on the needs of the user, proactively mitigating exclusion.
Through the process of design the human journey of using a service is mapped out end to end based on real insight helping to highlight shared challenges and opportunities for improvement. latest.question: Deputy Cathy Bennett asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation the basis on which it was decided to award excessive salary increases to the CEOs of many State bodies.
latest.reply:
On 27 June 2023, the Minister for Public Expenditure National Development Plan Delivery and Reform published the final review of the Report of the Independent Review Panel on Senior Public Service Recruitment and Pay Processes. The Panel made a range of findings and 38 recommendations. Among these recommendations was the establishment of a Review Body on Higher Remuneration to advise the Minister on total remuneration arrangements for senior posts in the Public Service and for Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) of CSBs. It further recommended that the CEOs of CSBs be prioritised for review by the recommended Body arising from the lack of an agreed mechanism to review rates and their exclusion from national pay agreements.
The Government subsequently established the Senior Post Remuneration Committee (SPRC) in March 2024 on an administrative footing and, as per the recommendations of the Report of the Independent Review Panel, the first task of the Committee was to perform a review of the remuneration arrangements for the CEOs of CSBs. In doing so Government was conscious of the scale, complexity and commercial responsibilities associated with leading major State companies, and their role in the management of critical national infrastructure and the delivery of significant investment programmes.
The SPRC’s review was independent, evidence-based and extensive. It represented the first systematic examination of Commercial State Body CEO remuneration since 2011 and involved broad co

latest.question: Deputy Cathal Crowe asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation if he will provide an update on plans to develop flood mitigating measures in the vicinity of Shannon town and Shannon Airport in County Clare.
latest.reply:
Shannon Town and its Environs are at risk of flooding from both coastal and fluvial (stream/river) sources. The main sources of coastal flooding risk are wave water overtopping of the embankment crest driven by strong winds during high tide periods and also through any potential breaches of the embankments. The main sources of fluvial flooding risk are the inadequate capacities of the existing drainage systems (surface water channels/culverts and pumping systems) and limited outflow capacities of the tidally affected outfall systems
The design options for the Shannon Town & Environs Flood Relief works are being progressed to protect 1,400 properties, including 1,237 residential and 163 commercial properties. A Value Engineering Review Workshop was held in January 2026 to consider all potential options for the Scheme. Meetings with the National Parks and Wildlife Services are also informing the potential options.
An additional Public Consultation Day took place in Q3 2026 where the emerging preferred Option was presented to the public, prior to the submission of a planning application.
On completion of the review and the feedback from the public consultation day, an emerging preferred option will be agreed by the project Steering Group, with the final report expected at the end of 2026. An Environmental Impact Assessment Report for the Scheme is projected to be completed by Q2 2027.
Clare County Council can apply to the OPW's Minor Flood Mitigation Works and Coastal Protection

latest.question: Deputy Pádraig O'Sullivan asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation the growth in public service numbers since 2021, by sector and by frontline and non-frontline grades, in tabular form; and how this data is informing his approach to the next public service pay agreement.
latest.reply:
The table below sets out the number of public service employees, in full time equivalent terms, by sector since 2021. The figures for 2026 are the latest available and reflect the position at end-June. This data, which was notified to my Department by the relevant organisations, is publicly available on the Department's website at http://databank.per.gov.ie/Public_Service_Numbers.aspx.
A breakdown by frontline and non-frontline grades is not available, as the classification of such grades varies across sectors and individual bodies.
Since 2021 there has been an overall growth of 15.9% or an average of 3% growth per annum.
The numbers data collated by DPER are a key input into how DPER estimates the costs associated with the next public service pay agreement. Costs of potential pay increases under a new public service pay agreement are determined using a whole of public service basis and are calculated using full-time equivalent staff numbers by salary band provided by relevant organisations in their quarterly returns to DPER.

latest.question: Deputy Matt Carthy asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation the measures he has introduced to ensure value-for-money in respect of public capital projects.
latest.reply:
My Department is responsible for the Infrastructure Guidelines. These set the value for money requirements and guidance for evaluating, planning and managing Exchequer-funded capital projects to ensure that vital infrastructure projects will be delivered on time and in a manner that ensures value for money through detailed evaluation, appraisal and planning. Management and delivery of investment projects and public services within allocation and the national frameworks, including the Infrastructure Guidelines, is a key responsibility of every Department, Accounting Officer and Minister.
Under the Accelerating Infrastructure Action Plan, a number of reforms to the Infrastructure Guidelines have been progressed and implemented under Action 23. In February, the following changes were implemented:
• In relation to Major Projects, the threshold will increase from €200m to €500m for sectors with a well established track record of delivery (Transport, Energy and Water)
• For all sectors, the External Assurance Process (EAP) will be replaced with a streamlined and time-bound internal review by the relevant Vote section in DPER; and
• Major projects at Approval Gate 2 will no longer need Ministerial approval and may now be approved solely by the Accounting Officer of the Government Department that is funding the proposed project.

latest.question: Deputy Barry Ward asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation the position regarding the work he is undertaking to ensure that all OPW owned buildings, structures and monuments have solar panels and other renewable energy provisions installed, where possible.
latest.reply:
The OPW are responsible for achieving the targets for building and transport emissions as set out in the Climate Action and Low Carbon Development (Amendment) Act 2021 and the annually updated Public Sector Climate Action Mandate, which commits Ireland to a strategic direction to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 51% by 2030 and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. As a National Estate Portfolio Lead (NEPL) OPW are part of the National Heat and Built Environment Taskforce that are working towards pathways for decarbonisation of the Public Sector Building Stock Portfolio.
The responsibility for achieving these targets is shared with other Departments that occupy OPW owned buildings. Sustainability and climate action are at the core of the Office of Public Works’ Statement of Strategy and the organisation is committed to a vision that strives for harmony between our built and natural environments. One key objective from the Office of Public Works’ Statement of Strategy is advancing climate action obligations and promoting the transition to a low carbon, climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable economy and the installation of solar panels and installing other renewable energy technologies, will significantly help towards achieving these objectives.

latest.question: Deputy Naoise Ó Muirí asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation whether the Government plans to move beyond annual capital investment targets and introduce a strategic framework, as recommended in the Future Forty report, with medium and long-term goals for infrastructure provision across housing, transport, energy and water services.
latest.reply:
The Government is fully committed to providing financial certainty for infrastructure projects needed to transform our housing, energy, water, transport, and health infrastructure over the next 10 years to ensure we meet the needs of our growing population.
The Review of the National Development Plan (NDP), published in July 2025, set out a €275 billion public capital investment programme to 2035, the largest in the history of the State. The plan set out Exchequer funded sectoral capital allocations of €102.4 billion for the years 2026 to 2030; and a further €100 billion for the period 2030 to 2035. In addition, an estimated total of €63 billion in non-Exchequer funding by commercial semi-state bodies, will be invested in capital expenditure. A further €10 billion, equity funding, has also been provided for the period 2026 to 2030 to support the delivery of large projects, such as electricity grid capacity, water and transport infrastructure.
The review increased overall allocations by an additional €34 billion relative to the previous 2021-2030 NDP.
This is the largest ever capital investment plan in the history of the State and will enable the delivery of thousands of new homes, increase Ireland's competitiveness, improve transport services, provide more childcare and school places, invest in children’s disability services and ensure better healthcare for all.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
